presentation: At Capgemini, I run digital projects for French government ministries and the public sector: application development, cyber risk assessments and sovereign solutions.
I built this site the way I run those projects: security as a starting requirement, explained choices and checks anyone can verify. Its code is public. My full background is on the résumé page.

securite.intro: A personal website does not need this level of protection. I still treated it as a sensitive service exposed to the Internet: the smallest possible attack surface, defence in depth and evidence for every measure.

mesures.texte: No third-party scripts or trackers, no exposed admin interface for this site. The server only accepts web traffic from Cloudflare and the domain is signed with DNSSEC.
Strict Content Security Policy with a fresh nonce on every page, two-year HSTS, framing forbidden and isolation headers. The server does not disclose any of its software.
Each service runs in a read-only container, without privileges, under a dedicated user. The application has no outbound access; only a separate mail service holds the mailbox credentials.

Personal links to the private area rely on 256-bit random tokens, stored as hashes, time-limited and revocable. An invalid link gets the same response as an expired one, and attempts are rate-limited.

Every change goes through a pull request: strict typing, unit and end-to-end tests, accessibility checks, code analysis with CodeQL and image scanning with Trivy. Actions are pinned by hash, dependencies are tracked by Dependabot, and deployment follows the merge automatically.
Server access by SSH key only, firewall, automatic banning and automatic security updates. Logs are deleted after 30 days. An automated external audit checks DNS, headers and security grades.

referentiels.intro: The guides and standards I relied on, and what I apply from them on this site. No body has certified it.

elements.nom: ANSSI recommendations for deploying Docker containers
elements.application: Read-only containers without capabilities or privilege escalation, internal network with no outbound access, images pinned by digest.

elements.nom: ANSSI configuration recommendations for GNU/Linux systems
elements.application: Minimal server, key-based SSH, firewall, automatic security updates, controlled logging.
TLS 1.2 minimum, encryption all the way to the server with a verified certificate, HSTS.

elements.nom: OWASP ASVS and OWASP cheat sheets
elements.application: Sessions through a __Host-, HttpOnly, SameSite cookie, cross-site request forgery protection, hashed tokens, rate limiting, uniform error responses.
Vulnerability management, logging, secure development and a pre-launch audit, modelled on the Annex A controls.
Data minimisation, published retention periods, cookie-free analytics, no IP address in the private area log.
Nonce and strict-dynamic policy, no unsafe-inline, checked on every change.
Two-year HSTS including subdomains; signed DNS zone.
Published security contact and a responsible disclosure policy in the repository.
Automated axe check of every page, contrast verified in both themes.

controles.libelle: Qualys SSL Labs, on all four site addresses
high-severity finding in the October 2026 audit

code.texte: The repository is public by choice: how a site is designed, secured and maintained says as much as what it displays. Every change is tracked, tested and analysed before it goes live.
